passes.summary: Rates up again (10-year 5.10%, a third tailed auction this week, Fed hike odds near 89%) and Nvidia's CEO gone. One take from 20 candidates: YETI short against XRT on a demand-led guide cut ahead of next week's retail reports. AMD was dropped after the challenge showed the pair doesn't express the rotation out of Nvidia.

signal.why: closed at 38.30, below the 20-day low 40.47, on 4.9x volume (-10.5%, -2.6 ATR); from a loose base: daily ranges of the 10 sessions before today 1.42x the 50 before; 50-day below the 200-day and falling (trend down)

proposals.reason: Guide cut on weaker US demand with the CEO flagging Q4 pressure; broke the 20-day low on 4.9x volume inside a downtrend, with analyst cuts still to come and retail reports next week.

reasoning.what_changed: -10.5% to 38.30 on 4.9x volume, -2.6 ATR, below the 20-day low 40.47; 50-day below a falling 200-day.
reasoning.story: Q3 on 11-12 before the open (8-K): sales $509.4M (+4%) against $523.1M expected; adjusted EPS $0.91 beat $0.84. FY adjusted sales growth cut to about 6% from 7-8%, EPS to $2.90-2.95 from $2.94-3.00, operating income growth to 7-9% from 10-12%. Direct-to-consumer -6% on weak US e-commerce and Amazon; the CEO cited more selective consumers and Q4 demand pressure in the US and Canada. Pre-print consensus target about $54, so cuts are still to come.
reasoning.chart: For: a breakdown on the heaviest volume of the setup list, in a downtrend, from a loose base. Against: -2.8 ATR from the 20-day and RSI 36, so some of the move is in; support at the 52-week low 34.90, 8.9% below.
reasoning.coming: PPI 11-13 8:30 AM ET; October retail sales and Home Depot 11-17; Target and TJX 11-18 and Walmart 11-19 (unconfirmed). The 5-session limit ends at the 11-19 close.
reasoning.case_against: The EPS beat, a 310 bp gross margin gain and about $350M of buyback authority (about 11% of the market cap at 38) give holders reasons to defend it. The challenge added more: adjusted sales were +6% and adjusted direct-to-consumer only -3%; wholesale and international each grew 19%; margin and free cash flow guidance were unchanged; the EPS cut is about 1.5%. Morgan Stanley ($48, 10-27) and UBS ($44) had already cut targets, so further cuts may be partly priced. Short interest is about 11% of float. XRT is equal-weight and small-cap heavy, and weak retail prints next week would hit the long leg. Why it didn't win: none of this contradicts the guide cut or the CEO's Q4 warning. The weakness is in YETI's own channels while its retailer customers grew, so a pair against retail expresses it.

proposals.wrong_if: Two or more brokers raise targets or upgrade on the margin story; the company announces an accelerated buyback; or the retail reports (retail sales and Home Depot 11-17, TJX and Lowe's 11-18, Walmart 11-19) describe improving discretionary demand and YETI regains 40.47.
proposals.hedge_why: Correlation 0.62, the best of 42 funds; beta 1.08, so equal dollars are close to market-neutral. The thesis is YETI's demand against retail in general.

proposals.reason: The challenge took it below the bar. Long AMD against SOXX doesn't express a rotation out of Nvidia: SOXX holds more AMD (about 9.3%) than NVDA (8.1%), and its other holdings (Broadcom, Micron) gained from the same move. The move wasn't specific to AMD either: Broadcom rose as much, and NVDA bought back most of a 13% gap. After hours the pair gave back about 1.5% as SOXX rose on Applied Materials' beat. AMD is up 45% since 11-05 and 2.5% under Oppenheimer's new $600 target. A long AMD against short NVDA would fix the pair, but the case for it would still rest on one day of flows.
